Criterion: Q1 — SER task and data origin
0 — not met: No emotion task on spoken utterances, or source cannot be established
0.5 — partly met: Speech-linked task but spoken origin/labels partly unclear
1 — met: Emotion recognition of spoken speech or clearly speech-derived transcript; audio, audio–text and justified speech-grounded settings accepted
Coding guidance: No penalty solely for having text or speech-centered context. Written-only sentiment is outside scope.

0.5 — partly met: Dataset named; mapping, split or preparation partly unclear
1 — met: Dataset provenance, classes, processing and sampling adequately reported
Coding guidance: Video-derived recording permitted; written text converted to TTS is not real emotional-speech evidence.

0.5 — partly met: Some details given, but split/validation or implementation ambiguous
1 — met: Dataset partition, evaluation unit, model and test protocol replicable in principle
Coding guidance: Avoid assigning full credit solely from accuracy or benchmark name.

0 — not met: Only claims of explainability or attention used for optimization
0.5 — partly met: XAI described but explanation target/model connection partly unclear
1 — met: A concrete XAI/reasoning method applied to an identified emotion prediction or relevant model component
Coding guidance: Modality weighting alone is not automatically a speech explanation.

0.5 — partly met: Only qualitative claim or limited output with ambiguous linkage
1 — met: Figure, table, concept score or generated rationale linked to emotion predictions from speech or speech-derived language
Required evidence: Specific page/figure, predicted class and evidence
Coding guidance: Do not treat confusion matrix, training curves or architecture alone as XAI.

1 — met: Appropriate SER metrics on stated test data with interpretable baselines/comparisons
Coding guidance: Compare model outcome and explanation separately.

1 — met: Interpretation with meaningful validation or sensitivity/robustness/fidelity test
Coding guidance: Natural-language rationale is observed explanation but not automatically faithful.
